errors.text: The proposed strain-rate range of 10^-4 to 10^2 s^-1 does not reconstruct the molecular-dynamics regime of 10^8 to 10^10 s^-1, so the claimed strain-rate insensitivity is assigned to a substantially different physical regime.

The dominant target mechanism is dislocation nucleation at vacancy clusters or disordered sites followed by Shockley-partial slip and stacking-fault formation; the hypothesis instead attributes yielding primarily to a large-activation-volume lattice-friction process and possible surface nucleation.
Surface nucleation is inconsistent with the target bulk periodic model, which has no free surfaces.
The required crystallographic anisotropy is not reconstructed: the <110>, <1-12>, and <-111> loading directions and the maximum yield stress along <-111> are omitted.
The material description introduces Co as a possible constituent even though the target alloy is FeNiCrMn.
